dimensions.assessment: Affects student athletes, prospective student athletes, higher education institutions nationwide, athletic conferences, interstate associations, and sports agents.
dimensions.evidence: No institution, conference, or interstate intercollegiate athletic association may restrict the ability of a student athlete to enter into a name, image, and likeness agreement.

dimensions.assessment: Completely reshapes college athletics governance by preempting state laws, capping compensation via pool limits, establishing mandatory institutional health and medical benefits, and barring employee status for student athletes.
dimensions.evidence: Notwithstanding any other provision of Federal or State law, no individual may be considered an employee of an institution... based on the participation of such individual on a varsity sports team

dimensions.assessment: Imposes significant financial and revenue-based requirements on institutions generating $20 million or more in college sports revenue, including mandated medical benefits, degree completion funds, and restrictions on student athletic fees.
dimensions.evidence: an institution described in this subsection if such institution reports... having generated not less than $20,000,000... in total revenue derived by the institution from the institution's intercollegiate athletics activities

dimensions.assessment: Creates comprehensive federal statutory rules for name, image, and likeness rights, amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 and the Sports Agent Responsibility and Trust Act, grants antitrust exemptions, and broadly preempts state laws.
dimensions.evidence: No State, or political subdivision of a State, may maintain, enforce, prescribe, or continue in effect any law, rule, regulation, requirement, standard, or other provision... that conflicts with this Act

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent federal standards, ongoing compliance reporting requirements every two and five years, and phased effective dates starting in 2026.
dimensions.evidence: take effect on July 1, 2026, and shall apply with respect to academic year 2026-2027 and each succeeding academic year.

missing_information: Exact monetary totals for the overall economic impact on athletic revenues across all NCAA institutions.
importance_detail.rationale: Sweeping legislation governing college athletics that establishes federal frameworks for name, image, and likeness rights, preempts state laws, exempts association rules from antitrust laws, sets institutional mandates, and alters higher education reporting.

related.title: Providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 4312) to protect the name, image, and likeness rights of student athletes and to promote fair competition with respect to intercollegiate athletics, and for other purposes; providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 1005) to prohibit elementary and secondary schools from accepting funds from or entering into contracts with the Government of the People’s Republic of China and the Chinese Communist Party, and for other purposes; providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 1049) to ensure that parents are aware of foreign influence in their child’s public school, and for other purposes; providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 1069) to prohibit the availability of Federal education funds for elementary and secondary schools that receive direct or indirect support from the Government of the People’s Republic of China; providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 2965) to require the Administrator of the Small Business Administration to ensure that the small business regulatory budget for a small business concern in a fiscal year is not greater than zero, and for other purposes; and providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 4305) to direct the Chief Counsel for Advocacy of the Small Business Administration to establish a Red Tape Hotline to receive notifications of burdensome agency rules, and for other purposes.

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The SCORE Act creates a federal framework for student athlete name, image, and likeness (NIL) agreements, sets rules for athletic associations, mandates certain benefits and minimum varsity sports for high-revenue college athletic programs, and preempts state laws concerning student athlete compensation and employment status.

affected_groups.effect: Gain federally protected rights to enter into NIL agreements and obtain agents, receive mandatory post-graduation medical benefits and degree completion assistance at high-revenue schools, are explicitly classified as non-employees, and are subject to association transfer and recruitment rules.

Higher-revenue institutions face new mandates regarding sports team minimums, medical benefits, and student fee restrictions, while all institutions are protected from state laws conflicting with this federal framework and receive antitrust compliance protection for association rules.

Empowered to create and enforce standardized rules governing NIL disclosures, recruitment, athlete transfers, agent registration, and revenue pool limits, provided they comply with specific diversity and governance structures.
Subject to federal disclosure rules, registration requirements, and a fee cap limiting endorsement contract charges to no more than 5 percent of the compensation provided.

key_provisions: Prohibits institutions, conferences, and athletic associations from restricting a student athlete's ability to enter into name, image, and likeness agreements, with certain exceptions for prohibited compensation or conflicts with school codes of conduct.

Mandates that institutions of higher education generating $20 million or more in annual athletic revenue provide comprehensive academic support, career counseling, medical and health benefits (including coverage for injuries up to 3 years post-separation), maintain grants-in-aid regardless of athletic performance, provide degree completion assistance, and maintain at least 16 varsity sports teams.
Establishes that student athletes cannot be considered employees of an institution, conference, or interstate intercollegiate athletic association based on their participation in sports.
Preempts state and local laws regarding student athlete compensation, payments, benefits, employment status, eligibility, and academic standards.

Grants interstate intercollegiate athletic associations the authority to establish and enforce rules regarding NIL disclosures, recruitment, transfer parameters, agent registration, and maximum pool limits for institution payments.

Imposes transparency and restriction rules regarding student fees used to support intercollegiate athletics, prohibiting institutions with high annual media rights revenues of $50 million or more from using student fees for athletic programs beginning in academic year 2028-2029.
Requires various federal studies and reports, including a Federal Trade Commission study on agent regulation and Comptroller General reports on compliance and the impact on Olympic sports.
missing_information: Exact dollar amounts for pool limits, as they depend on future calculations by athletic associations based on the 70 highest earning institutions.
Specific details on the exact outcomes or legislative recommendations of the required FTC and Comptroller General studies, which have not yet been conducted.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The SCORE Act creates a federal framework for student athlete name, image, and likeness (NIL) agreements, sets rules for athletic associations, mandates certain benefits and minimum varsity sports for high-revenue college athletic programs, and preempts state laws concerning student athlete compensation and employment status.
summary_detail.significance: The SCORE Act carries sweeping significance for the structure of collegiate athletics by replacing a patchwork of state laws with a uniform national framework, settling legal questions around employment status and NIL rights, and reshaping financial and operational mandates for high-revenue athletic programs.
